messages:
Jamie: Quick question — router precedence for multi-tenant requests: if we receive x-vpc-id + x-dedicated-pool + x-workspace-id headers, what's the intended resolution order? Specifically for Private endpoints where VPC binding exists. Should VPC binding always win, or can an authorized workspace override with dedicated-pool header? cc @Ben @Tara
Ben: My take: x-vpc-id should be top-level binding for private endpoints — it guarantees network and billing boundaries. Dedicated-pool header can win only if the request token includes a 'pool:override' scope (admin/console action). Otherwise fall back to x-workspace-id for workspace scoping.
Tara: Agree. Important: record which rule matched in telemetry (route.match_reason) so billing/quota/alerts are deterministic. Quota enforcement must use the final resolved pool id, not the incoming header.
Mike: For internal canaries we inject x-dedicated-pool from the console sometimes — we need a safe allowlist per origin so random clients can't escalate by spoofing headers.
Jamie: Proposed algorithm: if x-vpc-id present -> validate VPC binding -> resolve workspace(s) bound to that VPC and route to VPC-bound pool; else if x-dedicated-pool present AND token has pool:override -> route to that pool; else if x-workspace-id present -> route to workspace default pool; else -> shared pool. Also surface fallback reasons in the response headers for debugging.
Ben: +1. Add header scrubbing before logs to avoid leaking other customers' IDs. Also add console warnings if a canary header is used without allowlist entry.
Anita: For the Console UX: add a "routing audit" column in the request log view showing matched_vpc | matched_pool | matched_workspace and match_reason. That will speed up customer support/debugging.
deploy-bot: infra-check: gateway matcher unit tests passed (12/12).
Jamie: Example matcher config for RFC draft:
```
matchers:
  - if: headers.x-vpc-id && vpc.binding.exists
    target: vpc-bound-pool
    reason: 'vpc_binding'
  - if: headers.x-dedicated-pool && auth.scopes.contains('pool:override')
    target: headers.x-dedicated-pool
    reason: 'pool_override'
  - if: headers.x-workspace-id
    target: workspace-default-pool
    reason: 'workspace_header'
  - else:
    target: shared-pool
    reason: 'default_shared'
```
Tara: Looks good. I'll own telemetry tags (route.match_reason, matched_pool_id, matched_vpc) and add unit tests for tokens without override scope and one with spoofed header.
Ben: I'll own the gateway header allowlist + console warning flow.
Jamie: I'll draft the RFC and link tests/specs. Anyone want to pair on the telemetry schema? @Tara?
Tara: I'll take telemetry + console audit column.
Jamie: Thanks — filing RFC after lunch.
